clue.text: Cow moos, repeatedly expelling gas in Welsh valleys

indicators.note: expelling means throwing out, and repeatedly says it happens each time the gas turns up in the words

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen, a gas; it appears three times in the words, so all three go

explanation.surface: A cow lowing over and over while breaking wind as it grazes in the valleys of Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly expelling gas' strips every O (oxygen) out of COW MOOS, leaving a Welsh word that looks unpronounceable.
explanation.definitionFit: A cwm is the Welsh word for a valley or hollow, plural adding S; it is a favourite of crossword setters for its lack of vowels.

clue.text: Doctor left to collect Arachne's eyewash

indicators.note: to collect is to gather in, so the doctor-and-left pair takes the setter's contraction into its middle

parts.note: Arachne is the setter, so Arachne's can be read as 'Arachne has', the setter's own I'VE

explanation.surface: A doctor turns up to fetch the setter's lotion for sore eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters refer to themselves by their pseudonym; 'Arachne's' reads as 'Arachne has', i.e. I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is slang for nonsense or humbug, the same as senseless twaddle.

clue.text: Medical labs in Netherlands engaging retired bouncer

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the hidden letters are read from right to left
engaging means holding within, so the answer is held inside the run of words from Medical to Netherlands

explanation.surface: Dutch medical laboratories taking on a doorman who has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit backwards across 'medicaL LABS IN NETherlands'; 'engaging' marks the hiding and 'retired' the turnaround.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball used in a racket sport is made to spring off the ground, so it is a thing that bounces.

clue.text: Virginal Conservative on speed

parts.note: haste means speed or hurry

explanation.surface: An innocent Tory politician who happens to be high on amphetamines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speed' looks like the drug, but it simply means haste; 'on' just places one piece before the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone virginal has kept their sexual purity, which is to be pure and abstinent.

clue.text: One idiot about to go around and disperse depleted uranium, say

indicators.note: to go around is to turn back on itself, so the preceding three pieces are read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a nit (nitwit) is an idiot
CA, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: depleted means emptied, so only the outer letters of the word disperse remain

explanation.surface: A fool is about to spread depleted uranium around, a worrying prospect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go around' reverses the first three pieces to give ACTINI, and 'depleted' keeps only the ends of 'disperse'. 'Depleted uranium' reads as one phrase but splits across two jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Uranium belongs to the series of radioactive elements from actinium to lawrencium, so it is one example of that group.

clue.text: Interminable sex act finally taking toll

indicators.note: interminable here means without its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: bonk is British slang for an act of sex

indicators.note: finally points to the final letter of the word taking

explanation.surface: An endless bout of lovemaking that eventually takes its toll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interminable' cuts the final K from BONK (British slang for sex) to leave BON, and 'finally' adds the G that ends 'taking'.
explanation.definitionFit: To toll is to ring a bell slowly, and a bell's ringing note is described by this sound word.

clue.text: Fan of Elizabeth Taylor is eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters of Taylor and is are rearranged

explanation.surface: An admirer of the film star Elizabeth Taylor is a strange sort.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Elizabeth Taylor' as one name; it splits, with 'Elizabeth' the Queen and 'Taylor is' the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of the monarchy, such as one devoted to Queen Elizabeth, backs the Crown.

clue.text: Kid brother cheers up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from bottom to top, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks, i.e. cheers

explanation.surface: A younger brother brightens up his sibling.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for thank you, the same sense as 'cheers'.
explanation.definitionFit: A badly behaved child is commonly called this, and a kid is a child.

clue.text: Wore thick pants, something Protestants have

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish or poor, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wore thick trousers, a habit Protestants are said to share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like trousers but is British slang for rubbish, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The so-called Protestant work ethic is the belief that diligent labour is a moral duty, a trait attributed to Protestants.

clue.text: Do parts of us smell?

indicators.note: parts means splits apart, so the word Do pushes into the middle of the possessive and separates it

parts.note: our means belonging to us, i.e. of us

explanation.surface: An anxious question about whether certain bits of the body give off a whiff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like the start of a question and 'parts' like a noun; in fact 'parts' is a verb, with 'Do' splitting the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: An odour is a scent or whiff, especially an unpleasant one.

clue.text: Prime Suspect's original episode cut short

indicators.note: original means the first, so the first letter of Suspect's is taken
cut short says the last letter is removed

parts.note: an event is an episode or occurrence

explanation.surface: The first instalment of the TV drama Prime Suspect was trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: Prime Suspect is a British TV crime series; 'Prime' splits off as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The number in question is divisible only by itself and one, making it a prime number.

clue.text: Asking RAF technicians about operation

indicators.note: about here means around, so the words go about the answer, which sits within them

explanation.surface: Someone queries the air force's engineers about a military operation.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'aSKING RAF Technicians'; 'about' is an unusual hiding signal, meaning the words lie around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Transplanting healthy tissue onto a burn or wound is a surgical procedure.

clue.text: According to Spooner, only that man Francis lives here

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words, the signal for an exchange of initial sounds

parts.note: solely means only
he refers to that man

explanation.surface: Spooner insists the Pope is the only one who resides in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the S and H sounds of SOLELY HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pope Francis is head of the bishopric of Rome, whose seat and government is known by this name.

clue.text: Vacuous, happy folk in Maidenhead

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so only the outer letters of happy are kept

parts.note: men are folk, people

explanation.surface: Empty-headed cheerful people live in the Berkshire town of Maidenhead.
explanation.walkthrough: Maidenhead is a town west of London, but here it means virginity's membrane.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidenhead is an old word for virginity and also the membrane associated with it.

clue.text: Well-oiled Indian bowling team

parts.note: IND is an abbreviation for Indian
in lawn bowls and curling a rink is a team of players

explanation.surface: An Indian side of bowlers who are thoroughly drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: In bowls a team of four is called a rink; 'Well-oiled' is slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Being drunk, intoxicated after alcohol, is described by this idiom.

clue.text: Stubborn butcher met dire end

indicators.note: to butcher is to hack about or mangle, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An obstinate butcher came to a grim finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butcher' looks like a noun for the person, but it is a verb, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stubborn is resolute and immovable in purpose.

clue.text: Well-groomed male observed guards

indicators.note: guards means holds protected inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: kept means observed, as in kept a promise

explanation.surface: A man is seen to be watching over some guards, all neatly turned out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'observed' looks like 'seen', but means KEPT as in 'kept the rules'.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat and tidy in appearance, it is a back-formation from unkempt.

clue.text: Dame Edna's initial career as terrible mother

indicators.note: to career is to rush about wildly, so these letters are thrown into a new order
initial means the first letter of Edna's

explanation.surface: Dame Edna Everage's early career as a dreadful mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' looks like a noun for working life, but as a verb it signals rearranging DAME plus E (Edna's initial).
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this sorceress killed her own children, making her a dreadful parent.

clue.text: Sophisticated editor backing British broadcasting

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the abbreviation for editor is reversed

parts.note: on air means currently broadcasting

explanation.surface: A refined editor supports British broadcasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like supporting, but it signals reversing ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone suave and urbane has polished, confident manners.

clue.text: Edges away from very pale woman

indicators.note: edges away from means the edge letters are removed

parts.note: ashen means very pale, like ash

explanation.surface: A very pale woman cautiously sidles away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edges away' reads as a verb of movement, but means trimming the ends off ASHEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The female pronoun stands for a woman.

clue.text: Making dopey son search for love online

parts.note: e-dating is looking for romance through internet sites

explanation.surface: Looking for romance on the internet leaves one's son in a daze.
explanation.definitionFit: Administering a sedative makes someone drowsy and slow.

clue.text: Art of jazz trumpeter Armstrong touched us magically at the start

indicators.note: at the start points to the first letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: The skill of jazz trumpeter Louis Armstrong moved us wonderfully from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' looks like skill, but it is a first name: Art Tatum, the jazz pianist.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Tatum was a celebrated American jazz pianist, so the clue gives his first name and genre.

clue.text: Prevented from winning, VIP wept

parts.note: a nob is an important or upper-class person
bled is used loosely for wept, shed blood or tears

explanation.surface: A celebrity cried after being stopped from winning.
explanation.walkthrough: NOB is British slang for a toff or VIP.
explanation.definitionFit: To nobble a horse or competitor is to tamper with it so it cannot win.

clue.text: Decent chap keeping member in trousers?

definitions.note: trousers are one item of clothing, an example, signalled by the question mark

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a decent chap
an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A respectable man keeping his private part inside his trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' hints at something ruder, but it is just an ARM.
explanation.definitionFit: Trousers are an article of clothing, an example of the general term.

clue.text: Class describing imaginary number for Einstein?

indicators.note: describing means drawing around, so the class goes round the number

parts.note: a genus is a class or kind
i is the mathematical symbol for the square root of minus one

explanation.surface: A lesson on imaginary numbers for Albert Einstein.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in its geometric sense of drawing a line around.
explanation.definitionFit: Einstein is the archetypal brilliant mind, an example of the term, signalled by the question mark.

clue.text: Surviving by hiding in a tent abroad

indicators.note: hiding in means concealed inside, so the multiplication sign goes within the rearranged letters
abroad means scattered widely, so the letters of a tent are rearranged

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as by (three by four)

explanation.surface: Getting through by sheltering in a tent overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' shuffles A TENT to ETANT, and 'hiding in' puts X inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that still exists has lasted to the present, as documents or species can.

clue.text: Spill the beans and reveal one's unmarried

definitions.note: read as 'one who is unmarried', a noun phrase for a person

parts.note: to sing is slang for to inform or confess
to let on is to reveal or disclose

explanation.surface: Confess and admit that you are not wed.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is not married or in a relationship is a single person.

clue.text: Cries of old boy wearing socks inside out

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the outer pair goes around the old boy
inside out says take the inside away, leaving the outer letters of socks

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: Weeping from a former pupil who has put his socks on inside out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside out' means the inside is out, leaving the S and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Weeping noisily, crying with gulps, is the plural noun here.

clue.text: Lascivious look of Bluebeard oddly vanishing

indicators.note: oddly vanishing means the odd-numbered letters disappear, leaving the even ones of Bluebeard

explanation.surface: The lustful gaze of the wife-murderer Bluebeard fading away curiously.
explanation.definitionFit: A lecherous sideways glance, a sly or lustful look, is this word.

clue.text: Spy provides this home phone number

parts.note: in means at home
TEL is the abbreviation for telephone number

explanation.surface: A spy provides a home phone number.
explanation.definitionFit: Intelligence, the secret information an agent gathers, is shortened to this word.

clue.text: Six excluded from Liberal whip

indicators.note: excluded from means taken out of, so the Roman six is removed

parts.note: lavish means liberal, generous
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Six people are thrown out of the Liberal party by its whip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' and 'whip' look like party politics; a whip enforces party discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog or strike with a cane or thong is the same act, and the thong itself shares the word.

clue.text: Pickle and cheese sandwiches start to niff

indicators.note: sandwiches means holds between, so the cheese encloses a letter

parts.note: Brie is a French cheese

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of niff

explanation.surface: Pickle and cheese sandwiches that begin to smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'niff' is British slang for a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Salty water used for preserving food is a pickling liquid.

clue.text: Gutless Amazon repellently exploit workers — they make you sick

indicators.note: repellently means in a disgusting way, here treating the letters so they are mixed into a new order
gutless means with the insides removed, so just the outer letters of Amazon remain

parts.note: to use someone is to exploit them
worker ants are the stock crossword workers

explanation.surface: Cowardly Amazon disgustingly exploits its staff, which is sickening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutless' looks like 'cowardly' but empties the company name; 'repellently' then shuffles the result with the synonym for exploit into NAUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Substances that bring on vomiting are emetics, also called by this medical term.
